The petitioner herein claims that he has raised objection dated 8.8.2022 under Section 3-H(3) with regard to entitlement of respondent no.4 to claim compensation for acquisition of plot no.584 in Khata No.247 (New No.232) situated at Village Manoharpur, Tehsil Mahavan, District Mathura,
under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.

The petitioner claims to be recorded tenure-holder of the plot in question and is claiming that the respondent no.4 is seeking disbursement of compensation on the basis of mutation application filed by him based on succession claiming to be the son of Babu heirs and legal representatives of the original tenure-holder Rewati son of Kishan Lal.

sentences.text: On a query made by the court, learned counsel for the petitioner could not place before us the correct position with regard to mutation of their name in the revenue records.

From the objection filed by the petitioner appended at page '35' of the paper book as annexure-5, it is evident that the original tenure holder of plot no.584 in Khata No.247 (New No.232), Village Manoharpur, Tehsil Mahavan, District Mathura was Rewati son of Kishan Lal.
The mutation case no.71 TM/2002 was decided on the basis of an un-registered Will in the name of the objector/petitioner and respondent no. 5 to 9 herein.
A recall application filed by Raja Ram namely respondent no.4 on account of which, the order of mutation was recalled.
Another mutation case had been filed by Raja Ram namely respondent no.4 which were both clubbed and decided by the order dated 24.5.2011.
The order dated 24.5.2011 is not before us.
The contention in the writ petition is that the respondent no.4 has no right, title or interest in the land in question, therefore, cannot be looked into.

The statement in the objection filed by the petitioner and private respondents no.5 to 9 before the competent authority under Section 3-H(3) of the National Highways Act, 1956 does not give the clear picture about the rights of the rival claimants..
We therefore, cannot issue any mandamus as prayed for.
The writ petition is accordingly, dismissed as misconceived.
It is open for the petitioner to agitate his claim before the Competent Authority.
